result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers correctly see the tour as a list of interface features rather than a path to sending a first invoice, and both name the steps to cut or defer. A is more careful: it won't make up an invoice time ('Fill in the time only if you've measured it'), it states its activation assumption, and it adds useful details like a sample client and a nudge to fix the navigation before writing help text. B does propose a check (drop-off at steps 2–4), but it asserts an unmeasured '2 minutes' and guesses that the tour shows '1 of 7'. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers diagnose the tour as an interface inventory, centre the fix on sending a first invoice, and cut steps by name. B is the stronger design overall: it has a guided real invoice with at most three coach marks, a sample client, the bank prompt moved to after the first invoice is sent, and a way to replay the guide. A is better at hedging. It points out that step-1 skippers never see the later steps and suggests checking drop-off at steps 2–4, while B states the cause more confidently and only checks where users abandon the new flow.
